cluster_label: Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty Act 2012
title: Regulatory Exemption Authority under Section 126(1)

qa_pairs.scenario: As the construction of the Rampal 1320 MW power project enters a critical phase in June 2024, our procurement team is finalizing the shipment of specialized plant and equipment from abroad. We are carefully reviewing the latest fiscal measures to ensure our customs filings are accurate and cost-effective. Given the strategic national importance of this energy infrastructure, we need to clarify the specific fiscal concessions available. What is the maximum customs duty rate applicable to the imported plant and equipment for this power project under the new regulatory framework?
qa_pairs.question: What is the maximum customs duty rate applicable to the imported plant and equipment for this power project under the new regulatory framework?
qa_pairs.answer: The customs duty rate is reduced to a maximum of 5 percent, provided all compliance conditions are met.

qa_pairs.scenario: In July 2024, as our country faces another surge in dengue cases, our medical supply firm is rushing to import essential test kits and diagnostic reagents to meet the overwhelming public demand. We are working closely with the customs authorities to expedite the clearance process while ensuring we follow the correct legal procedures for tax adjustments. To ensure our documentation is legally sound, we need to identify the specific legislative foundation for these government notifications. Which legal acts provide the authority for the government to issue notifications regarding tax and duty adjustments for these medical items?
qa_pairs.question: Which legal acts provide the authority for the government to issue notifications regarding tax and duty adjustments for these medical items?
qa_pairs.answer: The authority is provided by Section 25(1) of the Customs Act 2023, Section 126(1) of the Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty Act 2012, and Section 76(1) of the Income-tax Act 2023.

qa_pairs.scenario: As a lead developer appointed under the Hi-Tech Park Authority Act, our firm is currently importing a large consignment of specialized construction and technical goods required for the ongoing development of our designated zone in June 2024. We are preparing our customs declaration and want to ensure we correctly apply the relevant fiscal incentives provided for such projects. We need to understand how the benefit is structured to minimize our tax liability. How is the customs duty exemption calculated for developers appointed under the Hi-Tech Park Authority Act?
qa_pairs.question: How is the customs duty exemption calculated for developers appointed under the Hi-Tech Park Authority Act?
qa_pairs.answer: Developers are granted a partial exemption on customs duty for any amount that exceeds 5 percent of the value of the imported goods.

qa_pairs.scenario: Our company is preparing to launch a state-of-the-art amusement park, and in June 2025, we are expecting the arrival of several containers filled with specialized rides and safety equipment. As we coordinate with our clearing agents, we are reviewing the current SROs to determine exactly how much of the import duty we are liable to pay. We need to be certain about the specific regulatory limit that triggers our exemption. What is the threshold for customs duty exemption on imported amusement park equipment as of June 2025?
qa_pairs.question: What is the threshold for customs duty exemption on imported amusement park equipment as of June 2025?
qa_pairs.answer: Exemption is granted on the portion of the import duty that exceeds a ten percent ad-valorem rate.

qa_pairs.scenario: Our pharmaceutical manufacturing facility has recently expanded its capabilities, and in June 2025, we are importing a series of high-grade chemical compounds necessary for the domestic production of Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (API). We are fully certified by the Directorate General of Drug Administration and are keen to utilize the government’s fiscal support for local API production. We need to confirm the extent of the duty relief available for these specific raw materials. Are these chemical compounds eligible for a full exemption from customs duty?
qa_pairs.question: Are these chemical compounds eligible for a full exemption from customs duty?
qa_pairs.answer: Yes, provided the manufacturer is certified by the Directorate General of Drug Administration and meets the specified conditions, they are granted exemption from all customs duty.

qa_pairs.scenario: Our legal compliance team has been tracking the evolution of tax policy in Bangladesh, specifically focusing on the regulatory powers granted under Section 126(1) of the VAT and Supplementary Duty Act 2012. Over the past year, we have noticed shifts in the underlying legislative framework that support these exemptions as new statutes have been enacted. To ensure our long-term tax planning remains compliant, we need to document these shifts in the primary partner acts. How has the primary partner act for Section 126(1) changed over the observed period?
qa_pairs.question: How has the primary partner act for Section 126(1) changed over the observed period?
qa_pairs.answer: The legal basis has transitioned from referencing the Customs Act 1969 to the Customs Act 2023.

qa_pairs.question: Which legal transition occurred regarding the foundational authority for Section 126(1) of the Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty Act 2012 exemptions?
options: From the Income-tax Act 2023 to the Customs Act 2023
From the Customs Act 1969 to the Customs Act 2023
From the VAT Rules 2016 to the Customs Act 1969
From the Customs Act 2023 to the Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty Act 2012
qa_pairs.answer: From the Customs Act 1969 to the Customs Act 2023
qa_pairs.explanation: The context indicates that the legal basis for Section 126(1) transitioned from referencing the Customs Act 1969 (used in pre-2024 instruments like SRO 112-AIN/2021) to the Customs Act 2023 (used in SRO 182-AIN/2024 and subsequent 2024/2025 orders).

qa_pairs.question: When did the government first formally implement the new Customs Act 2023 framework in conjunction with Section 126(1) of the VAT and Supplementary Duty Act 2012?
qa_pairs.explanation: The timeline and clauses confirm that SRO 182-199/2024, issued on 2024-06-06, established the first set of exemptions under the new Customs Act 2023 framework.

qa_pairs.question: Which of the following sectors saw an expansion of tax exemptions under the SRO 190-218/2025 series issued on June 2, 2025?
qa_pairs.explanation: According to the 'EVOLUTION DIMENSIONS' and the 2025-06-02 timeline entry, the SRO 190-218/2025 series introduced a broad expansion of exemptions for new sectors including E-bikes and Lithium batteries.

qa_pairs.question: What action was taken by the government regarding SRO 170-AIN/2024/22/Customs on June 2, 2025?
options: It was amended to include new H.S. codes
It was repealed in the public interest
It was extended for another fiscal year
It was consolidated into the Customs Act 2023
qa_pairs.answer: It was repealed in the public interest
qa_pairs.explanation: SRO 237-AIN/2025/59/Customs, issued on 2025-06-02, explicitly states that the notification SRO 170-AIN/2024/22/Customs (dated May 29, 2024) is hereby repealed.

qa_pairs.misaligned_context: In 2021, the government issued an SRO citing the Customs Act 2023 and Section 126(1) of the Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty Act 2012 to grant industrial tax exemptions.
qa_pairs.question: Why is the legal basis mentioned in the provided 2021 context passage factually inconsistent with the evolution of Bangladeshi customs policy?
qa_pairs.conflict: The passage cites the Customs Act 2023 for a 2021 regulatory action, but the Customs Act 2023 did not exist as the legal basis at that time.
qa_pairs.answer: The context is misaligned because, prior to the transition to the Customs Act 2023, the legal framework for customs exemptions in 2021 relied on the Customs Act 1969. As evidenced by SRO 112-AIN/2021/01/Customs (dated May 24, 2021), the government utilized the Customs Act 1969 in conjunction with Section 126(1) of the Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty Act 2012.

qa_pairs.misaligned_context: On June 6, 2024, the government updated its regulatory framework for power projects by referencing the Customs Act 1969 and Section 126(1) of the VAT and Supplementary Duty Act 2012.
qa_pairs.question: What is the correct legal basis for the power project exemptions established on June 6, 2024, and why is the provided context incorrect?
qa_pairs.conflict: The context incorrectly attributes the June 2024 SROs to the Customs Act 1969, whereas the transition to the Customs Act 2023 had already occurred by that date.
qa_pairs.answer: The context is incorrect because the legal basis transitioned to the Customs Act 2023 by June 2024. According to SRO 182-AIN/2024/34/Customs, issued on June 6, 2024, the government exercised its authority under Section 25(1) of the Customs Act 2023 and Section 126(1) of the Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty Act 2012.

qa_pairs.scenario: A manufacturer has been operating under tax exemptions granted by the government since 2022. They noted that their original notifications cited Section 19(1) of the Customs Act 1969. By mid-2024 and through 2025, they observed that new government notifications and amendments regarding similar exemptions began citing Section 25(1) of the Customs Act 2023 instead.
qa_pairs.question: How has the primary legal basis for the government's authority to grant customs duty exemptions evolved from the 2022 notifications to those issued in 2024 and 2025?
qa_pairs.answer: The legal basis transitioned from Section 19(1) of the Customs Act 1969 to Section 25(1) of the Customs Act 2023.

qa_pairs.question: Starting from the initial establishment of exemptions under the Customs Act 2023 framework on June 6, 2024, what major expansion occurred one year later regarding the scope of these exemptions?
qa_pairs.answer: One year later, on June 2, 2025 (SRO 190-218/2025), the government broadly expanded exemptions to include new sectors such as E-bikes and Lithium batteries, while simultaneously rescinding older, redundant notifications.
